The deceased, identified as 29 year-old Thapelo Walter Maphanga, together with his two armed accomplices attacked a local shop, pointed firearms at everybody, demanded money. According to police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Moatshe Ngoepe, Maphanga hails from Mablejan village in Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga Province. No arrests have been made at the time of going to press and investigations are continuing. Four killed and five injured Nkhensani Nkhwashu- A motor vehicle accident left four people dead and five injured along the Eiland public road outside Letsitele last Wednesday. Police spokesperson, Lieutenant Colonel Moatshe Ngoepe said, a Toyota quantum kombi lost control and overturned. Ngoepe said the kombi was transporting nine students who were coming from the University of Venda after registration back to their homes in Nelspruit, Mpumalanga province. "Four passengers being two men and two woman around their 30's died instantly," said Ngoepe. He said the five injured passengers together with the 35 year-old driver were taken to Letaba Hospital with serious injuries. "The cause of this accident is still unknown at this stage but Police investigations are still continuing," concluded Ngoepe. The University of Venda issued a statement about the incident sending their condolences to the bereaved families. The statements states that out of the four deceased persons one was a former student and two were prospective students. The University Deputy Vice-Chancellor Operations, Dr Jannie Zaaiman said that the University is saddened by the loss and have tremendous empathy for the bereaved families. Our prayers for strength are with them, he said. The University counselling centre will provide counselling service to the survivors and next of kin of the deceased. THE Limpopo Economic Development Department (LEDET) officially launched the annual Marula Festival at Sefapane Lodge and Safaris in Phalaborwa on Friday. This year marks the 11th edition of the festival since its inception in The festival is used as a platform for locals to showcase products they have made from the marula fruit such as jam, hand and body lotion, soaps, cooking oil, nuts and atchar. The music festival will be held over a period of two weekends, starting from February LEDET's MEC, Seaparo Sekoati said the festival will not only benefit Ba-phalaborwa but it will also benefit nearby towns as well. "The objective of this festival at its inception was not just about fun but was to fight poverty and unemployment among our people, to develop local tourism and hospitality industries through the promotion of Marula month," said Sekoati. 13 cooperatives across the province will benefit from the festival which the government continues to support and help market beyond the borders of the province. Our involvement as government in the facilitation of registration of these Cooperatives had positive spin-offs on investment into the industry and the employment of rural community members who assisted in harvesting and transportation of the fruit annually, depending on the order from the organizers of the Marula festival," said Sekoati. He also added that they will not relent until the living standard in the province has improved. The town of Phalaborwa, because of its tourism profile and close proximity to other major tourist destinations including the world s renowned Kruger National Park, has been declared a permanent home for hosting the annual Marula festival. The town has a well-developed infrastructure, a top class airport and golf course, a wide variety of tourists accommodation, tourism products and numerous game lodges in close proximity. It is easily packaged with products around Hoedspruit, Tzaneen, Modjadjiskloof, Magoebaskloof and Giyani. This location and setting make Limpopo Marula Festival a major attraction for locals, domestic and international tourists.the MEC has also vowed that a recording studio will be opened from funds that will be gathered throughout the event. Modjadjiskloof ly al vir 'n geruime tyd onder krag- en wateronderbrekings, selfs wanneer daar nie beurtkrag geskeduleer is nie. Volgens inwoners (en selfs sommige werkers van die Groter Letaba Munisipaliteit wat naamloos wil bly) is hierdie meerendeels te danke aan 'n gebrek aan instandhouding. Wanneer die elektriese infrastruktuur wel misluk, is die pa en seun span van Mike's Electrical, Mike en Dylan van der Spuy, gewoonlik daar om te help. Teen geen vergoeding doen hulle wat hulle kan om die dorp se kragtoevoer te herstel. Verlede week het die gemeenskap van Modjadjiskloof hulle soos een man agter die Van der Spuys geskaar om die kraguitdagings die hoof te bied nadat onderhandelinge tussen die bestuur van die Groter Letaba Munisipaliteit en sy werkers weereens skipbreuk gely het. Hoewel die Herald berig het dat werkers die krag gesny het kan dit nou reg gestel word dat dit Van der Spuy self was omdat hy bang was die lyn word aangeskakel terwyl hy daaraan werk. Die geldelike dispuut is na arbitrasie verwys en werkers moes weer die volgende dag gaan werk. Dit het egter steeds nie die elektriese probleme opgelos nie en Span Van der Spuy moes weer aan die werk spring. Die Munisipale bestuur en die gemeenskap het tot 'n vergelyk gekom en daar is ooreengekom om dadelik, met die volle ondersteuning en hulp van Munisipale werkers die krag probleem te begin oplos. "SOME of the greatest accomplishments throughout history are marked by our capacity to push through incredible amounts of physical and mental pain to reach new heights and new goals" - Derek Lauber. Stanford Lake College took two teams to compete in the Adventure Challenge for Schools in Zambia from December 4-8. Nine teams from 3 countries, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia competed in the event. Adventure racing is a multi-disciplined, nonmotorised sport where mixed gender teams of 4 compete. It takes months of gruelling dedicated planning and training to prepare for these events. Last year s event was held at Mulungushi Dam, Zambia - 200km North East of Lusaka. Two Stanford Lake College (SLC) teams, 4 teachers and several parents left on the 30th of November 2015, making their way through Botswana and Zimbabwe to finally set up camp 4 days later on the banks of the Mulungushi Dam in Zambia. It was an exciting four days of fast paced intensive activities. Day 1 activities were at Mulungushi Dam. The teams moved on water via canoe between the different activities -mountain biking, canoeing, kayaking, rock climbing, bouldering, high water jumps and various initiative exercises. Day 2 was spent in a gorge just below the hydro plant with activities such as gorge walking, running, hiking through river beds, abseiling, slack lining over water pools, more water jumps, Tyrolean traverse, raft building, rock pool diving, problem solving, cooking, map work and orienteering were undertaken. The Grand Challenge was over the last 2 days and was a continuous race of about 100km which included all the activities they had done during the first few days, all as one event. Not a lot of rain and high temperatures made things even more difficult! After four days of racing, various activities and a lot of blood, sweat and gears; it was a close finish between Zimbabwe s Falcon College senior team (Bushtic Gladiators) who took 1st place overall, with the SLC senior team (Ubuntu) in 2nd place by 21minutes. The SLC Junior team (Tshanduko) came home in 3rd place 25 minutes behind their senior team. Highlights of the long journey, were a river cruise down the Zambezi river at Kasane on the way there, white river rafting down the mighty Zambezi River at Victoria Falls.With 3 members doing it in kayaks (and YES, there is water at Victoria Falls, contrary to all the photos and rumours!) and mountain biking in the Matopos just outside Bulawayo (a World Heritage site) on the way home - and this was all just for fun. A huge thank you to all the sponsors: Trophy Toyota, Trappers Trading in Mall of the North, PPS in Tzaneen, Falconwood Water and Adventure Zone in Victoria Falls. Then all the teachers and the parents who came along for the adventure, their assistance and support was truly appreciated, the two teams could not have done it without them. Thank you. Well done to the 2 teams, Ubuntu and Tshanduko on finishing the year off on a high note and for their dedication throughout the year to put in all the hard training that was essential to achieving excellent results. THE Limpopo Economic Development Department (LEDET) officially launched the annual Marula Festival at Sefapane Lodge and Safaris in Phalaborwa on Friday. This year marks the 11th edition of the festival since its inception in The festival is used as a platform for locals to showcase products they have made from the marula fruit such as jam, hand and body lotion, soaps, cooking oil, nuts and atchar. The music festival will be held over a period of two weekends, starting from February LEDET's MEC, Seaparo Sekoati said the festival will not only benefit Ba-phalaborwa but it will also benefit nearby towns as well. "The objective of this festival at its inception was not just about fun but was to fight poverty and unemployment among our people, to develop local tourism and hospitality industries through the promotion of Marula month," said Sekoati. 13 cooperatives across the province will benefit from the festival which the government continues to support and help market beyond the borders of the province. Our involvement as government in the facilitation of registration of these Cooperatives had positive spin-offs on investment into the industry and the employment of rural community members who assisted in harvesting and transportation of the fruit annually, depending on the order from the organizers of the Marula festival," said Sekoati. He also added that they will not relent until the living standard in the province has improved. The town of Phalaborwa, because of its tourism profile and close proximity to other major tourist destinations including the world s renowned Kruger National Park, has been declared a permanent home for hosting the annual Marula festival. The town has a well-developed infrastructure, a top class airport and golf course, a wide variety of tourists accommodation, tourism products and numerous game lodges in close proximity. Verlede week het die gemeenskap van Modjadjiskloof hulle soos een man agter die Van der Spuys geskaar om die kraguitdagings die hoof te bied nadat onderhandelinge tussen die bestuur van die Groter Letaba Munisipaliteit en sy werkers weereens skipbreuk gely het. Die geldelike dispuut is na arbitrasie verwys en werkers moes weer die volgende dag gaan werk. Dit het egter steeds nie die elektriese probleme opgelos nie en Span Van der Spuy moes weer aan die werk spring. Die Munisipale bestuur en die gemeenskap het tot 'n vergelyk gekom en daar is ooreengekom om dadelik, met die volle ondersteuning en hulp van Munisipale werkers die krag probleem te begin oplos. Daar is besluit om nie die probleem met die ondergrondse kabels te probeer regmaak nie, maar om eerder nuwe oorhoofse kabels bo-gronds te span. Dit sou nie net die kragtoevoer tot die dorp herstel nie maar ook help om verdere kragonderbrekings te verhoed wanneer daar, soos in die verlede 'n paar druppels reën val. "SOME of the greatest accomplishments throughout history are marked by our capacity to push through incredible amounts of physical and mental pain to reach new heights and new goals" - Derek Lauber. Stanford Lake College took two teams to compete in the Adventure Challenge for Schools in Zambia from December 4-8. Nine teams from 3 countries, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia competed in the event. Adventure racing is a multi-disciplined, nonmotorised sport where mixed gender teams of 4 compete. It takes months of gruelling dedicated planning and training to prepare for these events. Last year s event was held at Mulungushi Dam, Zambia - 200km North East of Lusaka. Two Stanford Lake College (SLC) teams, 4 teachers and several parents left on the 30th of November 2015, making their way through Botswana and Zimbabwe to finally set up camp 4 days later on the banks of the Mulungushi Dam in Zambia. It was an exciting four days of fast paced intensive activities. Day 1 activities were at Mulungushi Dam. The teams moved on water via canoe between the different activities -mountain biking, canoeing, kayaking, rock climbing, bouldering, high water jumps and various initiative exercises. Day 2 was spent in a gorge just below the hydro plant with activities such as gorge walking, running, hiking through river beds, abseiling, slack lining over water pools, more water jumps, Tyrolean traverse, raft building, rock pool diving, problem solving, cooking, map work and orienteering were undertaken. The Grand Challenge was over the last 2 days and was a continuous race of about 100km which included all the activities they had done during the first few days, all as one event. Not a lot of rain and high temperatures made things even more difficult! After four days of racing, various activities and a lot of blood, sweat and gears; it was a close finish between Zimbabwe s Falcon College senior team (Bushtic Gladiators) who took 1st place overall, with the SLC senior team (Ubuntu) in 2nd place by 21minutes. The SLC Junior team (Tshanduko) came home in 3rd place 25 minutes behind their senior team. Highlights of the long journey, were a river cruise down the Zambezi river at Kasane on the way there, white river rafting down the mighty Zambezi River at Victoria Falls.With 3 members doing it in kayaks (and YES, there is water at Victoria Falls, contrary to all the photos and rumours!) and mountain biking in the Matopos just outside Bulawayo (a World Heritage site) on the way home - and this was all just for fun. A huge thank you to all the sponsors: Trophy Toyota, Trappers Trading in Mall of the North, PPS in Tzaneen, Falconwood Water and Adventure Zone in Victoria Falls. Then all the teachers and the parents who came along for the adventure, their assistance and support was truly appreciated, the two teams could not have done it without them. Thank you. Well done to the 2 teams, Ubuntu and Tshanduko on finishing the year off on a high note and for their dedication throughout the year to put in all the hard training that was essential to achieving excellent results. THE Limpopo Economic Development Department (LEDET) officially launched the annual Marula Festival at Sefapane Lodge and Safaris in Phalaborwa on Friday. This year marks the 11th edition of the festival since its inception in The festival is used as a platform for locals to showcase products they have made from the marula fruit such as jam, hand and body lotion, soaps, cooking oil, nuts and atchar. The music festival will be held over a period of two weekends, starting from February LEDET's MEC, Seaparo Sekoati said the festival will not only benefit Ba-phalaborwa but it will also benefit nearby towns as well. "The objective of this festival at its inception was not just about fun but was to fight poverty and unemployment among our people, to develop local tourism and hospitality industries through the promotion of Marula month," said Sekoati. 13 cooperatives across the province will benefit from the festival which the government continues to support and help market beyond the borders of the province. Our involvement as government in the facilitation of registration of these Cooperatives had positive spin-offs on investment into the industry and the employment of rural community members who assisted in harvesting and transportation of the fruit annually, depending on the order from the organizers of the Marula festival," said Sekoati. He also added that they will not relent until the living standard in the province has improved. The town of Phalaborwa, because of its tourism profile and close proximity to other major tourist destinations including the world s renowned Kruger National Park, has been declared a permanent home for hosting the annual Marula festival. "SOME of the greatest accomplishments throughout history are marked by our capacity to push through incredible amounts of physical and mental pain to reach new heights and new goals" - Derek Lauber. Stanford Lake College took two teams to compete in the Adventure Challenge for Schools in Zambia from December 4-8. Nine teams from 3 countries, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia competed in the event. Adventure racing is a multi-disciplined, nonmotorised sport where mixed gender teams of 4 compete. It takes months of gruelling dedicated planning and training to prepare for these events. Last year s event was held at Mulungushi Dam, Zambia - 200km North East of Lusaka. Two Stanford Lake College (SLC) teams, 4 teachers and several parents left on the 30th of November 2015, making their way through Botswana and Zimbabwe to finally set up camp 4 days later on the banks of the Mulungushi Dam in Zambia. It was an exciting four days of fast paced intensive activities. Day 1 activities were at Mulungushi Dam. The teams moved on water via canoe between the different activities -mountain biking, canoeing, kayaking, rock climbing, bouldering, high water jumps and various initiative exercises. Day 2 was spent in a gorge just below the hydro plant with activities such as gorge walking, running, hiking through river beds, abseiling, slack lining over water pools, more water jumps, Tyrolean traverse, raft building, rock pool diving, problem solving, cooking, map work and orienteering were undertaken. The Grand Challenge was over the last 2 days and was a continuous race of about 100km which included all the activities they had done during the first few days, all as one event. Not a lot of rain and high temperatures made things even more difficult! After four days of racing, various activities and a lot of blood, sweat and gears; it was a close finish between Zimbabwe s Falcon College senior team (Bushtic Gladiators) who took 1st place overall, with the SLC senior team (Ubuntu) in 2nd place by 21minutes. The SLC Junior team (Tshanduko) came home in 3rd place 25 minutes behind their senior team. Highlights of the long journey, were a river cruise down the Zambezi river at Kasane on the way there, white river rafting down the mighty Zambezi River at Victoria Falls.With 3 members doing it in kayaks (and YES, there is water at Victoria Falls, contrary to all the photos and rumours!) and mountain biking in the Matopos just outside Bulawayo (a World Heritage site) on the way home - and this was all just for fun. A huge thank you to all the sponsors: Trophy Toyota, Trappers Trading in Mall of the North, PPS in Tzaneen, Falconwood Water and Adventure Zone in Victoria Falls. Then all the teachers and the parents who came along for the adventure, their assistance and support was truly appreciated, the two teams could not have done it without them. Thank you. Well done to the 2 teams, Ubuntu and Tshanduko on finishing the year off on a high note and for their dedication throughout the year to put in all the hard training that was essential to achieving excellent results. İranın Ehtiyaclı Məhbuslara Yardım və Qan Pulu Işləri üzrə qeyri hökumət təşkilatının xəbər saytının (ipro.ir) məlumatına görə, hazırda 1800-dən çox kişi mehriyyə ödəyə bilmədiyi üçün həbsxanalardadır. Qeyd edək ki, İranda çox vaxt dəbdəbəli və bahalı olan toy məclislərinin pulunu bəyin ailəsi ödəyir. Boşanan qadına “mehriyyə”ni isə ər qaytarmalıdır. Əksər vaxt böyük məbləğlər olur və kişilər boşanmadan sonra bu məbləği ödəyə bilmədikləri üçün neçə illər borc içində qalmalı olurlar. İran Parlamentinin ötən il təsdiqlədiyi qanuna əsasən, boşanma zamanı qadına ödəniləcək mehriyyənin miqdarı 110 "Bahar-Azadi" qızıl sikkə təyin olunub. Ölkədə mövcud qanunvericiliyə görə, mehriyyə kəbin kəsilərkən ailə quran tərəflər arasında müəyyən olunur. Kəbinə xüsusi qeyd olan mehriyyənin miqdarı boşanma zamanı qadına ödənilməli məbləğ olaraq əsas götürülür. 110 sikkədən artıq mehriyyənin təyin olunması isə ərin maddi durumundan asılıdır. (Hər bir sikkə 1 milyon tümən – yəni təqribən 300 dollardır). Bu həm sikkə olaraq və ya onun dəyərində torpaq, vəsait və digər şeylər olaraq qadına ödənilə bilər. Lazımi ödənişin edilməməsi həbsxana cəzası ilə nəticələnə bilər. İranın Vətəndaşlıq Vəziyyəti Aktlarının Əhalinin siyahıya alınması bürosunun direktoru Əli Əkbər Məhzun deyir ki, İranda hər saat başına 19 boşanma halı qeydə alınır. 2014-cü ildə 163 573 boşanma qeydə alınıb. Boşananların ən yüksək faizinin paytaxt Tehranda qeydə alındığı bildirilir
